name: Strike the center
description: Hit the opponent’s central pawns with your own pawns.

lessons.prompt: Black’s e5 pawn holds the center. Strike it with a pawn.
hints: Which pawn can attack e5 right now?
The knight on f3 already supports d4.
lessons.explanation: 3.d4 (the Scotch) hits e5 at once. After 3...exd4 4.Nxd4 White has open lines and easy development.

lessons.prompt: You played c3 for a reason. Use it.
hints: c3 supports a pawn on d4.
lessons.explanation: 5.d4 is the point of c3: it attacks e5 and the c5 bishop, aiming for a big pawn center. Stockfish rates the quiet 5.d3 about the same, but d4 is the principled strike.

lessons.prompt: White has two pawns in the center. Challenge them.
hints: e6 was played to support a pawn move.
lessons.explanation: 2...d5 is the whole idea of the French: e6 supports d5, which attacks e4 straight away. Without it White keeps a big center for free.

lessons.prompt: Same idea, different support. Strike the center.
hints: d5, backed by c6, attacks e4.
lessons.explanation: 2...d5 is why Black played c6: the pawn on d5 is supported and attacks e4, and the c8 bishop stays free.

lessons.prompt: Open the position: strike in the center.
hints: Black’s c5 pawn watches d4. Challenge it anyway.
d4 offers your d-pawn for Black’s c-pawn.
lessons.explanation: 3.d4 (the Open Sicilian) trades White’s d-pawn for Black’s c-pawn. After 3...cxd4 4.Nxd4 White leads in development and has open lines for the pieces.
